name: FreshBooks
summary: Invoicing and accounting aimed at freelancers and service businesses, priced by billable clients.
best_for: freelancers and small service firms who bill time and want invoicing that chases payment for them — the client cap is generous enough at Plus for most one-person businesses
skip_if: you have more than a handful of clients and only need invoicing — the client cap is what pushes you up the ladder here, and flat-priced invoicing tools do not care how many clients you have
honest_knock: Two things multiply the number you first see. The promotional rate is 90% off for three months, so Lite is $23 rather than $2.30 from month four. And the meter is billable clients, not invoices or revenue: Lite stops at five, which a freelancer with a handful of retainers passes in their first good quarter, and the step to fifty clients is $43. Then people cost extra on top at $11 each, so a two-person studio on Plus is $54 a month rather than $43. Payroll is a separate $40 plus $6 a head, which is the line most people miss when they compare this against a bookkeeping tool that includes it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month for three months, then $23/mo on Lite
pricing.notes: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page) Every amount is unchanged since 1 August 2026. The prices shown are 90% off for three months. Lite $2.30 a month promotional, $23 regular, 5 billable clients. Plus $4.30 promotional, $43 regular, 50 billable clients. Premium $7 promotional, $70 regular, unlimited clients. Select is quote-only. Team members are $11 a month each on every tier, with 2 included on Select. Two add-ons sit in the fine print: Advanced Payments $20 a month and Payroll $40 a month plus $6 per user. The page prints the promotional saving beside each tier — $62.10 on Lite, $116.10 on Plus, $189.00 on Premium — which is exactly three months of the difference and confirms the discount runs three months and no longer. Separately, there is a 30-day free trial, and FreshBooks promises a full refund if you contact them within 30 days of purchase.

sessions.what: Daan started the 30-day trial; everything after that was measured inside the account. The first question the protocol asked was whether the trial takes a card, because their pricing page does not say. It does not — but the answer is on the signup page, not the pricing page, which is a small lesson in where vendors put the reassuring sentence.
findings: No card for the trial. The signup page states it plainly — “Try it free for 30 days. No credit card required. Cancel anytime.” — and the form asks only for an email address and a password. The pricing page, where you would actually look, says nothing about it.

The prices inside the account are not the prices on the pricing page. The public page leads with the promotional rate, currently a limited-time 90% off for three months. The in-app upgrade screen quotes the real thing: Lite $23, Plus $43, Premium $70 a month, with a Yearly toggle marked “Save 10%”. Sign up on the strength of $2.30 and the first screen you see afterwards is $23.
Two add-ons ride along on every tier, and they are easy to miss: Team Members at $11 per user a month, and Advanced Payments at $20 a month. They are listed under Lite, Plus and Premium alike.

Removing FreshBooks branding from the emails your client receives is not a paid feature — it is a quote-only one. It appears only on the top “Let's Talk” tier, alongside lower card fees and two included team members. On Lite, Plus and Premium your invoice mail carries their brand.

The client ceiling that decides the tier is not testable during the trial. Lite stops at 5 clients, Plus at 50, Premium unlimited — but the trial runs with full features, as the upgrade screen says in as many words (“Upgrade to a paid plan to continue using all of FreshBooks' great features”). We fed the client importer a six-client CSV and it accepted the file and moved straight to field matching, with no limit warning at the point where a Lite account would have stopped. So the meter that will actually bite you is the one you cannot feel while you are evaluating.
Prices are shown in USD on a Netherlands account, and the plan screen carries the note “Features vary by region.”

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
